Part B : data Frames and Conditional Statements

B1. Create a data frame students with 8 rows and these colums (use stringAsFactors = FALSE; sex is "M" or "F"):
```{r}
#B1
students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana",
           "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
print(students)
```

B2. Display he structure, dimentions, colunm names,a nd summary of the students.
```{r}
#B2

str(students)
dim(students)
names(students)
summary(students)


```
B3. Add the Colunm avaerage = the mean of midterm and final for each students, rounded to the to 1 decimal.

```{r}
#B3
students$average <- round(
  (students$midterm + students$final) / 2,
  1
)
print(students)


```

B4. Add a logical colunm passed that is TRUE when average >= 70 and attendance >=75.
```{r}
#B4
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 &
                   students$attendance >= 75

print(students)


```

B5. Using ifelse(), and a colunm standing with these values based on average:

```{r}
#B5

students$standing <- ifelse(
  students$average >= 90, "Honors",
  ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support")
)

print(students)
```

B6 : Write a function classify (score) that uses an if/ else if/ else chain and returns "Distinction" for 85 or above,"Merit" for 70 to 84, "PASS" for 50 to 69, "Fail" below 50. Test it with sapply (c(90, 73, 55, 40,), classify) and print the result.
```{r}

classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

result <- sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)
print(result)

```


Part C: rbind() and cbind()

C1.Create a data frame new_students with two students. Its columns must match the original, including average, passed and standing, computed the same way:
• id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92
• id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80
Use rbind() to append them to students, saving the result as students_all. 

```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
new_students$average <- round(
  (new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1
)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 &
                       new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(
  new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
  ifelse(
    new_students$average >= 75, "Good","Needs Support"
  )
)
students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
print(students_all)
```
C2.Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6). Use cbind() to attach it to students_all as a column named quiz. Confirm the result is still a data frame with class().
```{r}
#C2

quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)

print(students_all)
print(class(students_all))
```
C3 Create the matrix m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final) and use rbind() to append a final row containing the column means, labelled "mean"

```{r}
#C3
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
mean_row <- matrix(colMeans(m), nrow = 1, dimnames = list("mean", colnames(m)))

m <- rbind(m, mean_row)
print(m)
```

C4. In a comment (2-3 sentences), explain what error rbind() produces if the data frames have different column names, and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatch()

tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL }).
```{r}
bad <- data.frame(
  student_id = 11,
  student_name = "Kai"
)
safe_result <- tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
print(safe_result)

# When attempting to combine data frames with mismatched column names, rbind() 
# stops execution and throws an error stating that the "names do not match previous names." 
# Using tryCatch() intercepts this error, prints a custom diagnostic message instead of crashing, and safely returns NULL.
```

Part D: Subsetting 

D1. Extract the name column in three ways: $, [["name"]], and [ , "name"].
```{r}

print(students_all[["name"]])

# Method 3: Row-and-column indexing
```


D3 Using logical subsetting, select students with attendance above 90.


D4.  Using subset(), select students of sex "F" in section "A" or "C" whose final is at least 75; return only name, section and final.
```{r}
result_D4 <- subset(
  students_all,
  sex == "F" & section %in% c("A", "C") & final >= 75,
  select = c(name, section, final)
)

```

D5. Use which.max() and which.min() to report the name of the student with the highest and lowest average.
```{r}
highest_index <- which.max(students_all$average)
lowest_index <- which.min(students_all$average)

cat("Highest average:", students_all$name[highest_index],
    "-", students_all$average[highest_index], "\n")
cat("Lowest average:", students_all$name[lowest_index],
    "-", students_all$average[lowest_index], "\n")
```

D6. Sort students_all by average in descending order, then print the top 3 rows.
```{r}

  order(students_all$average, decreasing = TRUE),
]
top_three <- head(students_sorted, 3)
print(top_three)
```

E1. Convert section and sex in students_all to factors with factor(). Print levels() of each.
```{r}

students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)

print(levels(students_all$section))
print(levels(students_all$sex))
```

E2. Use table() to count students per sex and per section.
*Try the two-way table of sex by section: table(students_all$sex, students_all$section). What is the output?

E4 Create a new factor sex_label from sex using factor() with levels = c("F", "M") and labels = c("Female", "Male"). Add it to students_all and print its levels().
```{r}
students_all$sex_label <- factor(
  students_all$sex,
  levels = c("F", "M"),
  labels = c("Female", "Male")
)
5
print(students_all$sex_label)
print(levels(students_all$sex_label))
```

E5.Print summary() of sex_label. Then, using logical subsetting and mean(), print the mean average for each level of sex_label.
```{r}
print(summary(students_all$sex_label))
for (gender in levels(students_all$sex_label)) {
  selected_averages <- students_all$average[
    students_all$sex_label == gender
  ]
  cat(
    "Mean average for", gender, ":",
    round(mean(selected_averages), 1),
    "\n"
  )
}
```
